title: Land Revenue Permanent Settlement
definition: The Permanent Settlement, introduced in 1793 by Lord Cornwallis, was a land revenue system that fixed the tax liability of land in perpetuity with the zamindars, converting them into hereditary landowners while reducing cultivators to mere tenants.
importanceInUpsc: Crucial for both Prelims (chronology, geographical spread, key figures like John Shore and Cornwallis) and Mains (GS-1 Modern Indian History, impact of British economic policies on Indian agriculture, commercialization, rural indebtedness, and peasant uprisings).
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts, economic rationale, and operational mechanisms of the Permanent Settlement.
Evaluate spatial distribution, financial outcomes, and socio-economic transformations across Bengal, Bihar, Orissa, and Varanasi.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims statements and structure comprehensive analytical Mains answers.
prerequisites: Grant of Diwani Rights to the East India Company
